system.name: Cloudflare OS
system.description: A company's own AI productivity environment on Cloudflare Workers, where people chat with a code-writing agent, have it build small private apps called gadgets, share them, and reach outside services through gatekeepers that log every action and hold side effects for approval.

corpus.included: The cloudflare/cloudflare-os repository at the revision below and its history since 2026-05-29: the kernel (workshop-backend, workshop-shared), the web app, the router, the gatekeeper packages gatekeeper-github (the representative driver), gatekeeper-mcp, gatekeeper-mcp-portal, gatekeeper-context and gatekeeper-scheduler, the shared libraries, bundled blueprints, docs, plans, scripts and CI configuration.
corpus.excluded: Dependencies (pnpm-lock.yaml, vendored PDFium), generated output (worker-configuration.d.ts, generated wrangler.jsonc, routeTree.gen.ts), secrets, and the packages gatekeeper-cloudflare, gatekeeper-confluence, gatekeeper-email, gatekeeper-gitlab, gatekeeper-google, gatekeeper-homeassistant, gatekeeper-linear, gatekeeper-microsoft, gatekeeper-notion, gatekeeper-pagerduty, gatekeeper-slack, gatekeeper-spotify, gatekeeper-supabase, gatekeeper-websearch, gatekeeper-x and gatekeeper-zoominfo: drivers for individual outside services, variants of one driver contract; gatekeeper-github stays in as the representative driver.

consumers.name: User
consumers.description: A person at the company who signs in to the deployment to get work done with the agent and with gadgets, including in workspaces and gadgets other people shared with them.

consumers.name: Deployment admin
consumers.description: A person named in the deployment's list of admins, who configures the deployment for everyone, investigates users and workspaces, and reads the admin audit log.

providers.name: Cloudflare OS
providers.description: One company's deployment of Cloudflare OS, which its people open in a browser as one product.

parts.name: Workshop web app
parts.why: A single-page client that presents the Kernel's capabilities and hosts gadgets and gatekeeper apps in sandboxed frames; it keeps no state of its own, so it is part of the interfaces Workshop web app, Admin panel and Gatekeeper apps.

parts.name: Router
parts.why: The public origin, which passes requests on by path to the Kernel, the gatekeepers and the web app's files (packages/router/src/index.ts); routing machinery.

parts.name: Gatekeeper kit, MCP library and configurator runtime
parts.why: Libraries the gatekeeper variants build on (gatekeeper-kit, mcp-shared, configurator-ui); the gatekeeper owns policy and assembly.

parts.name: PDF renderer
parts.why: A stateless Worker with no route and no storage that draws PDF pages for one excluded driver; a library in its own isolate.

parts.name: Bundled blueprints
parts.why: Gadget source code the Kernel installs as blueprints on a deployment's first request; content, the built-in Blueprint resources.

parts.name: Gadgets
parts.why: User-written apps the Kernel runs in sandboxes; their code and data are the user's, and to consumers they are the Gadget resource.

parts.name: Shared libraries
parts.why: Typed storage, Office file readers and shared React UI (typed-storage, office-content, ui): libraries.

parts.name: Diagnostics libraries
parts.why: Server logging, metrics, tracing and frontend error reporting (observability, error-reporting): diagnostics, engineering tooling listed in excluded.

parts.name: Engineering tooling
parts.why: The API schema generator, test suites, evaluations, scripts and CI work on the system itself, so they sit outside the perimeter and are listed in excluded.

components.name: Kernel
components.description: The server at the heart of a deployment, which keeps users, workspaces, chats, gadgets, blueprints and the deployment's settings, runs the agent and gadgets in sandboxes, and decides who may reach what.

serves.area: Keep the deployment up to date

parts.name: API front
parts.why: PublicApiImpl and AuthenticatedApiImpl in server.ts authenticate the WebSocket and pass requests on to the user account and the workspace; they hold no state.

parts.name: Sign-in attempt
parts.why: PendingLogin relays a session token from a gatekeeper sign-in flow to the waiting browser; its state is that token in transit, a step of signing in.

parts.name: Device session handoff
parts.why: A step of signing a native app in; the staged credential lives in the user account.

parts.name: AI model access
parts.why: Adapters to AI model providers and AI Gateway, with built-in model gatekeepers that keep nothing and pass a gadget's model calls on; which models are enabled comes from Admin settings.

parts.name: Web fetch gate
parts.why: FetchLoopback passes every untrusted fetch on to the public web after the workspace decides it (authorizeFetch).

parts.name: Loopbacks
parts.why: Entrypoints that pass calls from sandboxed code back into the workspace.

parts.name: Blueprint catalog store
parts.why: KV and R2 storage for published blueprints, written by the workspace, admin settings, the API front and the user account, each for records it creates.

parts.name: Outside-service clients
parts.why: Adapters to the notification service, Browser Rendering and the deploy service (notification-service.ts, browser-export.ts, deployment-updates.ts), each placed with the component that calls it.

parts.name: Diagnostics
parts.why: Analytics, client error reports, logging and agent tracing (analytics.ts, client-errors.ts, observability.ts, agent-tracing.ts): engineering tooling, listed in excluded.

components.name: User account
components.description: One person's account object, which keeps their identity and sessions, connected accounts, AI model settings and usage, workspace list, blueprint library, notification devices and private unread state.

parts.name: Sign-in and sessions
parts.why: Kept in the account's one store and changed by the same class's methods.

parts.name: Connected accounts registry
parts.why: Kept in the account's one store; the credentials themselves are the gatekeeper's.

parts.name: AI model settings
parts.why: Kept in the account's one store and changed by the same class.

parts.name: Usage and billing
parts.why: The daily count and the billed Cloudflare account are kept in the account's one store; the usage checker only reads them.

parts.name: Outputs index
parts.why: Kept in the account's one store, filled from each workspace.

parts.name: Workspace list and shared-workspace records
parts.why: Kept in the account's one store and changed by the same class.

parts.name: Blueprint library
parts.why: Kept in the account's one store and changed by the same class.

parts.name: Unread state and notifications
parts.why: Kept in the account's one store; pushes go out through the notifications client.

parts.name: Admin user view
parts.why: Keeps nothing and returns the account's records to admins field by field through a narrowed host type.

parts.name: Connect callback and user selection exchange
parts.why: Entrypoints that pass a gatekeeper's callbacks and a selection ticket on to the account.

components.name: Workspace
components.description: One workspace's object, which keeps its chats, gadgets and their code history, connections, actions, hooks and sharing, runs its agent and gadgets, and decides what each caller may do there.

parts.name: Observer ledger
parts.why: Its requirements live in the workspace host's action log; same store, same records.

parts.name: Auto-approval
parts.why: Decides whether an action may apply without a person, but marks the same action records the workspace host changes.

parts.name: Git store
parts.why: The workspace's storage for code history; first tested as a Kernel part in round 2, it belongs to the workspace.

parts.name: Worktree bindings and replicas
parts.why: RPC objects handed to sandboxed code and per-execution in-memory state.

parts.name: Gadget runtime and code execution
parts.why: How the workspace host runs gadgets and code in sandboxes and hands them bindings.

parts.name: Chat cache warming
parts.why: Provider behavior: resends a turn's last model request before the provider's cache expires.

parts.name: Admin workspace view
parts.why: A read view of the workspace's metadata for admins; keeps nothing.

components.name: Workspace host
components.description: The core of a workspace, which keeps its chats, gadgets, connections, action log and hooks, runs gadgets and the agent's code in sandboxes, and serves the workspace's API.

components.name: Agent
components.description: The code-writing agent loop, which decides how each chat turn runs: what it asks the model, which tools it calls and in what order, and when it retries or compacts the history.

components.name: Sharing
components.description: The workspace's permission graph, which keeps its collaborators and share links and decides each person's effective access.

components.name: Admin settings
components.description: The deployment-wide settings object, the only writer of the deployment's settings, model catalog, standard formats and featured blueprints, which also installs bundled blueprints and checks for updates.

serves.area: Keep the deployment up to date

parts.name: Settings store
parts.why: Kept in the one AdminSettings store and changed only by its methods.

parts.name: Model catalog
parts.why: GatewayModels merges stored settings with the suggested catalog and keeps nothing.

parts.name: Admin API
parts.why: AdminApiImpl passes calls on to the settings object, the directory, the audit log and the views.

parts.name: Featured blueprints and output formats
parts.why: Kept by the same settings object, beside the settings.

parts.name: Bundled blueprint installer and update check
parts.why: Steps run by the settings object.

parts.name: Admin writes
parts.why: admin-writes.ts computes the arguments a write takes; it keeps nothing.

components.name: Admin audit log
components.description: The deployment-wide record of admin actions, which records each setting change, inspection call and workspace write before it takes effect, and prunes by retention.

parts.name: Recording, listing and statistics
parts.why: All work on the one audit store, changed only by append.

parts.name: Text bounds
parts.why: cutAdminAuditText bounds text a user controls before it is stored; a helper.

components.name: User directory
components.description: The deployment-wide list of users and workspaces behind user search and the admin listings, fed by each account and workspace.

parts.name: Search table, admin listings and feeds
parts.why: One store by design, changed by one class.

components.name: Gatekeepers
components.description: The connectors, one Worker per outside service or built-in service, that hold connected accounts' credentials, give agents and gadgets narrow access to single resources, log every read, and hold every change for approval.

parts.name: Vendor entry
parts.why: Stateless; describes the connector and starts the account's connect flow.

parts.name: Verifier
parts.why: A token for a user that the connected account mints for observer checks.

parts.name: Sessions
parts.why: The RPC objects a resource gatekeeper hands out; part of its interface.

parts.name: Configurator UIs and management apps
parts.why: Clients in sandboxed frames that present an account's or a resource's capabilities.

parts.name: Connect pages and OAuth callback
parts.why: Steps of connecting an account.

parts.name: Kit, MCP library and configurator runtime
parts.why: Libraries the variants build on; the gatekeeper owns provider facts, policy and assembly.

components.name: Connected account
components.description: A gatekeeper's object for one connected account, with variants per connector, which keeps the account's credentials and grants and mints a resource gatekeeper for each resource granted.

parts.name: Credential record and connect handshake
parts.why: Kept in the account object's one store through kit libraries.

parts.name: Entrypoint, verifier and management APIs
parts.why: Pass calls on to the account object or to Context collections.

parts.name: Resource configurators
parts.why: Clients that present the account's resources for picking.

components.name: Resource gatekeeper
components.description: A gatekeeper's object for one granted resource, with variants per connector, installed inside the workspace, which keeps that connection's caches, action journal and simulated results and decides which calls are reads and which are held changes.

parts.name: Facet store
parts.why: One store per connection, changed only by the facet class.

parts.name: Sessions and outside-service clients
parts.why: The interface it hands out and adapters to the outside service.

parts.name: Kit modules
parts.why: Libraries for journals, simulation, cursors and observer tracking.

components.name: Event source
components.description: A gatekeeper's hook driver, with variants such as the GitHub webhook driver and the scheduler, which keeps each enabled hook's registration and decides when it fires.

parts.name: Hook controller
parts.why: Its state is only in props; it passes enable and disable on to the driver.

parts.name: Driver store
parts.why: One store per variant, changed only by the driver class.

parts.name: Event parsing and schedule computation
parts.why: Keep nothing.

components.name: Context collections
components.description: The Context Library's store of collections of documents and skills that agents read, with their sharing, libraries and public listing.

components.name: Collection
components.description: One collection's object, which keeps its documents, skills, grants and git mirror tokens and answers who may read or edit it.

components.name: Collection library
components.description: One account's index of the collections it created or was given.

components.name: Public collection registry
components.description: A sharing domain's list of public collections, the one writer of the snapshot sessions read.

outsideServices.name: AI model providers
outsideServices.description: The language model services, such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini and Workers AI, that chats and gadgets call directly or through Cloudflare AI Gateway.

outsideServices.name: Cloudflare API
outsideServices.description: Cloudflare's account API, which lists a user's Cloudflare accounts and their AI Gateway credit balance.

outsideServices.name: Notification service
outsideServices.description: The Cloudflare-operated service that delivers push notifications to a user's registered devices.

outsideServices.name: Deploy service
outsideServices.description: The service that installed the deployment, which answers whether a newer release exists.

outsideServices.name: Cloudflare Access
outsideServices.description: Cloudflare's identity proxy in front of some deployments, whose sign-in tokens the Kernel only verifies.

outsideServices.name: Browser Rendering
outsideServices.description: Cloudflare's headless browser service, used to print gadgets as PDF.

outsideServices.name: Public web
outsideServices.description: Public websites that the agent and gadgets may read under the workspace's fetch policy.

outsideServices.name: GitHub
outsideServices.description: GitHub, reached by the GitHub gatekeeper for sign-in, repositories, issues, pull requests and webhooks.

outsideServices.name: MCP servers
outsideServices.description: Any Model Context Protocol server whose endpoint a user pastes in.

outsideServices.name: MCP server portal
outsideServices.description: The organization's MCP portal, one administrator-configured URL behind which the approved MCP servers sit.

outsideServices.name: Cloudflare Artifacts
outsideServices.description: Cloudflare's git repository service, which mirrors Context Library collections as git repositories.

resources.name: Workspace
resources.description: A space owned by one user that holds chats, gadgets and connections, and can be shared.

resources.name: Chat
resources.description: A conversation with the agent in a workspace, holding its messages, tool calls and the code changes it proposes until they are merged.

resources.name: Gadget
resources.description: A small app in a workspace, with client and server code, its own storage and its bound connections, built by the agent or by hand.

resources.name: Connection
resources.description: An outside resource, such as one GitHub repository or one MCP server, introduced to a workspace through a gatekeeper so its agent and gadgets may use it.

resources.name: Action
resources.description: A change an agent or gadget asked a connection to make, held and simulated until a person approves or rejects it.

resources.name: Hook
resources.description: A callback through which a gatekeeper wakes a gadget, for a scheduled task or an outside event.

resources.name: Scheduled task
resources.description: A schedule that fires a gadget's callback after an interval, on a calendar rule or once.

resources.name: Blueprint
resources.description: A shareable copy of a gadget's code, with releases, from which anyone holding its link can create a gadget of their own.

resources.name: Collaborator
resources.description: A person given access to a workspace they do not own: to build in it, or to use or only view one gadget.

resources.name: Share link
resources.description: A link whose secret key gives whoever opens it a fixed grant on a workspace or a gadget, until it is revoked.

resources.name: Account
resources.description: A person's account on the deployment: identity, profile, sign-in method and onboarding state.

resources.name: Connected account
resources.description: A person's account at an outside service, connected through a gatekeeper that alone holds its credentials.

resources.name: Connector
resources.description: An outside or built-in service the deployment can connect to through a gatekeeper, with the kinds of resource it offers.

resources.name: AI model
resources.description: A language or decision model that chats and gadgets can use, offered by the deployment or added by a user with their own key.

resources.name: AI usage
resources.description: A user's free daily allowance of AI use and the Cloudflare account their further use is billed to.

resources.name: Unread state
resources.description: A user's private read positions and unread counts across the chats they follow.

resources.name: Context collection
resources.description: A collection of documents and skills that agents read: private and shareable, or public and edited by admins.

resources.name: Deployment settings
resources.description: The settings an admin changes for the whole deployment.

resources.name: Audit record
resources.description: A record of one admin action: a setting change, an inspection call or a workspace write.

resources.name: Deployment
resources.description: The running installation itself, with its release and whether a newer one is available.

resources.name: Workspace entry
resources.description: A user account's record of a workspace it owns or has opened, with its title, role, last activity and outputs.

resources.name: Directory entry
resources.description: The deployment-wide listing of a user or a workspace that user search and the admin listings read.

resources.name: Library entry
resources.description: An account's entry for a context collection it created or was given.

resources.name: Public collection entry
resources.description: A sharing domain's listing of one public context collection.

resources.name: Gateway request log
resources.description: AI Gateway's log of each model request, from which the Kernel reads its cost.

resources.name: Cloudflare account
resources.description: A user's Cloudflare account, with its AI Gateway credit balance.

resources.name: Device subscription
resources.description: A device registered to receive push notifications for a user.

resources.name: Release
resources.description: A release of Cloudflare OS that the deploy service can install.

resources.name: Access session
resources.description: A person's signed-in Cloudflare Access session, with their email.

resources.name: Browser session
resources.description: A headless browser launched to load and print a page.

resources.name: Web page
resources.description: A public page or document on the web.

resources.name: GitHub account
resources.description: A person's GitHub identity, with its verified email and granted scopes.

resources.name: GitHub repository
resources.description: A GitHub repository with its files, issues, pull requests and CI runs.

resources.name: Repository webhook
resources.description: A webhook registered on a GitHub repository, through which GitHub reports its events.

resources.name: MCP server
resources.description: A Model Context Protocol server and the tools it offers.

resources.name: Git repository
resources.description: A git repository hosted by Cloudflare Artifacts.

interfaces.name: Workshop web app
interfaces.description: The single-page web app at the deployment's address, in a browser or inside a native app shell, where people chat, build, use and share gadgets.

interfaces.name: Gatekeeper apps
interfaces.description: The management apps of some gatekeepers, such as the Context Library and Scheduled Tasks, opened inside the web app at /gatekeepers/<app>.

interfaces.name: Push notifications
interfaces.description: Notifications pushed to a user's registered devices when a chat they follow gets a message.

interfaces.name: Admin panel
interfaces.description: The /admin pages of the web app, shown only to deployment admins.

interfaces.name: API command line
interfaces.description: The `cf-os api` command, a generated client of the same API, which on a deployment only admins may use.

interfaces.name: gatekeeper contract
interfaces.description: The RPC contract every gatekeeper Worker implements for the Kernel: vendor, connected account, resource gatekeeper and hooks, with the approval queue the Kernel hands back.

interfaces.name: model provider APIs
interfaces.description: The HTTPS APIs of the model providers, AI Gateway's API and its logs, and the Workers AI binding.

interfaces.name: Cloudflare account API
interfaces.description: Cloudflare's REST API for accounts and AI Gateway credit balance.

interfaces.name: notification service API
interfaces.description: The notification service's signed HTTPS API for registering devices and publishing notifications.

interfaces.name: update check
interfaces.description: The deploy service's URL that answers which release is newest.

interfaces.name: Access identity tokens
interfaces.description: The signed token Cloudflare Access attaches to each request, which the Kernel verifies.

interfaces.name: Browser Rendering binding
interfaces.description: The binding through which the Kernel launches a headless browser.

interfaces.name: public HTTP fetch
interfaces.description: Outbound requests to the public internet, restricted to public addresses.

interfaces.name: GitHub API
interfaces.description: GitHub's OAuth, REST and git APIs, and the webhooks GitHub posts back.

interfaces.name: MCP endpoint
interfaces.description: A Model Context Protocol server's HTTP endpoint, with its OAuth discovery chain.

interfaces.name: MCP portal endpoint
interfaces.description: The organization's MCP portal URL, speaking the Model Context Protocol for each upstream server.

interfaces.name: Artifacts binding
interfaces.description: The binding through which the Context Library reads and writes git repositories in Cloudflare Artifacts.

interfaces.name: user account RPC
interfaces.description: The methods of a user's account object that other kernel objects call.

interfaces.name: workspace RPC
interfaces.description: The methods of a workspace object that other kernel objects call.

interfaces.name: workspace admin view
interfaces.description: The workspace's admin entry, reached only over the Durable Object binding, and the time-limited AdminWorkspaceView it returns.

interfaces.name: account admin view
interfaces.description: The account's admin entry, reached only over the Durable Object binding, and the AdminUserView it returns.

interfaces.name: directory RPC
interfaces.description: The methods of the user directory object: feeds, search and listings.

interfaces.name: audit log RPC
interfaces.description: The methods of the admin audit log object: append, list and stats.

interfaces.name: gatekeeper account contract
interfaces.description: The vendor and connected-account part of the gatekeeper contract: describe, connect, reconnect, revoke, configure, mint, verify, open an app and save a file, with the connect callback sent back.

interfaces.name: resource gatekeeper contract
interfaces.description: The resource gatekeeper's part of the gatekeeper contract, its agent-facing session types, and the approval queue the workspace hands it.

interfaces.name: hook contract
interfaces.description: The hook controller a gatekeeper hands the workspace to enable or disable a hook, and the hook initiator the workspace hands back for deliveries.

interfaces.name: account token methods
interfaces.description: A variant's own account methods that its resource gatekeeper calls for tokens and access checks.

interfaces.name: schedule driver methods
interfaces.description: The scheduler driver's methods for listing a workspace's or an account's schedules.

interfaces.name: Context Library management API
interfaces.description: The API behind the Context Library app: collections, documents, skills, sharing and git tokens.

interfaces.name: Context Library agent session
interfaces.description: The read session the agent gets for context: search, list and read.

interfaces.name: agent hooks
interfaces.description: The runAgent entry and the AgentHooks interface through which the agent reads and writes its chat in the workspace.

interfaces.name: sharing manager
interfaces.description: The methods of the workspace's sharing manager over its collaborators and share links.

interfaces.name: collection library methods
interfaces.description: The methods of an account's collection library object.

interfaces.name: public registry methods
interfaces.description: The methods of a sharing domain's public collection registry.

areas.name: Work with the agent
areas.description: Chat with the agent in a workspace, have it build and change gadgets, and use what it made.

capabilities.name: Create workspace
capabilities.takes: nothing
capabilities.gives: a new, empty workspace only its owner can open

capabilities.name: List workspaces
capabilities.takes: nothing
capabilities.gives: the user's own and shared workspaces, with owner, last activity and pin

capabilities.name: Edit workspace
capabilities.takes: a workspace and a new title or pin
capabilities.gives: the workspace with its new title or pin

capabilities.name: Delete workspace
capabilities.takes: a workspace the user owns
capabilities.gives: the workspace gone for everyone

capabilities.name: Start chat
capabilities.takes: a prompt, a model and optional attachments
capabilities.gives: a new chat whose agent turn has begun

capabilities.name: Send chat message
capabilities.takes: a message with optional attachments
capabilities.gives: the agent's next turn: its replies, tool calls and proposed changes

capabilities.name: Follow chat
capabilities.takes: a chat
capabilities.gives: the chat's history and the live stream of the agent's turn

capabilities.name: Stop agent
capabilities.takes: a chat whose agent is working
capabilities.gives: the turn stopped, with its work so far kept

capabilities.name: Merge chat changes
capabilities.takes: a chat with proposed changes
capabilities.gives: the changes merged into the workspace's gadgets

capabilities.name: Revert chat changes
capabilities.takes: a chat and the changes to undo
capabilities.gives: the chat's draft without those changes

capabilities.name: Update chat with latest code
capabilities.takes: a chat whose workspace has moved on
capabilities.gives: the chat's draft rebased on the workspace's current code

capabilities.name: Edit chat title
capabilities.takes: a chat and a title
capabilities.gives: the chat with its new title

capabilities.name: Delete chat
capabilities.takes: a chat
capabilities.gives: the chat removed, with any unmerged changes

capabilities.name: Create gadget
capabilities.takes: a title
capabilities.gives: an empty gadget in the workspace

capabilities.name: Use gadget
capabilities.takes: a gadget
capabilities.gives: the gadget's app running in a sandboxed frame, live with whoever else has it open

capabilities.name: Edit gadget code
capabilities.takes: file edits
capabilities.gives: the gadget's code with the edits

capabilities.name: Browse gadget code
capabilities.takes: a gadget and a commit
capabilities.gives: its files, commit log and changed paths

capabilities.name: Read gadget console logs
capabilities.takes: a gadget
capabilities.gives: the log lines its code writes as it runs

capabilities.name: Export gadget
capabilities.takes: a gadget and an export format
capabilities.gives: a file such as a PDF or a standalone HTML page

capabilities.name: List my outputs
capabilities.takes: nothing
capabilities.gives: the documents and other things the user made, across workspaces

capabilities.name: See who is present
capabilities.takes: a workspace
capabilities.gives: the people viewing it now, with their roles

areas.name: Review agent actions
areas.description: Decide on the changes agents and gadgets queued for approval, and on what they asked to reach.

capabilities.name: List actions
capabilities.takes: a workspace and a filter
capabilities.gives: its pending and past actions, each with what it would do

capabilities.name: Change action status
capabilities.takes: an action, approved or rejected
capabilities.gives: the action applied to the outside service, or withdrawn

capabilities.name: Set auto-approval
capabilities.takes: a connection and an action kind
capabilities.gives: a rule that applies actions of that kind without asking

capabilities.name: Answer agent request
capabilities.takes: the agent's request for a connection or for a web address the policy refuses, accepted or denied
capabilities.gives: the agent resumed with that access, or told no

areas.name: Connect outside services

capabilities.name: List connectors
capabilities.takes: nothing
capabilities.gives: the services the deployment can connect to, with the resources each offers

capabilities.name: Connect account
capabilities.takes: a connector and, for some, the resource types to grant

capabilities.name: Reconnect account

questions.question: Are the Context Library and Scheduled Tasks gatekeepers components of their own beside the connector drivers?
questions.answer: One component, Gatekeepers, with every package as a variant, rather than three components (Connectors, Context Library, Scheduled Tasks); the kernel registers and calls all of them through one contract (buildGatekeeperVendorMap, gatekeeper.ts) and names none of them, but the Context Library and Scheduled Tasks keep product state of their own and have their own apps, and the variant rule does not say whether a shared registration contract outweighs that.

questions.question: How should a component with variants be opened?
questions.answer: By the roles every variant implements in the shared contract (Connected account, Resource gatekeeper, Event source), plus the Context Library's collection store, which two roles of that variant reach, rather than by variant, which the variant rule forbids, or leaving Gatekeepers closed although its role objects each keep a store only they change; the method speaks of parts, not of variants' parts.

questions.question: Is the agent a component, although it keeps no state?
questions.answer: A component rather than a part of the workspace; it passes only on making decisions no other part makes (how a turn runs), and it has a typed seam (AgentHooks) that its comment says was extracted to avoid cyclic dependencies, not to enforce a boundary.

questions.question: Who owns the blueprint catalog in KV and R2?
questions.answer: A storage part of the Kernel shared by four writers (the workspace publishes, admin settings installs and features, the API front imports, the user account deletes orphans) rather than a component of its own or a merge of the writers; each writes records it creates, except orphan deletion after the owning workspace is gone, and the rule on shared stores speaks of parts that change each other's records.

questions.question: Is auto-approval a component inside the workspace?
questions.answer: A part of the Workspace host rather than a component; its comment calls it the single authority on applying an action without a person, which passes the decision test, but it marks the same action records the host changes, which the shared-store rule merges.

questions.question: Are the Context Library's per-account library and public registry components, or indexes of the collection?
questions.answer: Components (Collection library, Public collection registry) rather than storage of the collection, as the kernel's User directory is; both are indexes fed through their own methods by more than one part, and no rule says when an index fed by others becomes a component.

questions.question: Is `cf-os api` an interface of the deployment admin's boundary or engineering tooling?
questions.answer: An interface (API command line) of the Deployment admin boundary rather than only tooling; on a deployment it lets only admins sign in and its calls are labelled in the audit log, while on a dev server it is the team's test driver, and a tool used both with and on the system fits both sides of the tooling rule.

questions.question: Are collaborators and people holding a blueprint link separate consumers?
questions.answer: Folded into User with a permission attribute rather than separate consumers; their goals (use a shared gadget, copy a blueprint) are a subset of the user's, and the split rule needs diverging goals.

questions.question: Which Level 3 component relies on Cloudflare Access?
questions.answer: None: the boundary stays at Level 2 (Kernel) rather than being given to the User account; the token is verified by the API front in server.ts, which is a part that passes requests on, and no rule says where an outside service goes when only a part reaches it.

questions.question: Are gadgets components of the system?
questions.answer: The Gadget resource rather than components; a running gadget keeps state only it changes and is reached only through its API, but its code is the user's, written at run time, not part of this repository.

questions.question: Are a gadget's hooks and the scheduler's schedules one resource?
questions.answer: Two resources, Hook (the workspace's record, enabled in Connections) and Scheduled task (the scheduler's record, listed in the Scheduled app), rather than one; users act on them in different places, and the model gives no rule for two records of one thing kept by two providers that are not one name.

questions.question: Are the deployment's model catalog and a user's own models one resource?
questions.answer: One resource, AI model, seen differently by the user and the admin, rather than two; both are models chats and gadgets run, kept by different components.

questions.question: Where do documentation and plans sit in places?
questions.answer: Under tooling (Documentation) rather than with the components they describe; places allows no kind for documents, and docs describe several components at once.

questions.question: Where does the router sit?
questions.answer: Placed on the provider Cloudflare OS as a part that passes requests on, rather than under the Workshop web app interface or the Kernel; it routes to the Kernel, every gatekeeper and the web app's files alike.

questions.question: Is the PDF renderer part of this map?
questions.answer: A library part of Cloudflare OS rather than a component; it keeps no state, makes no decision for a consumer, and only an excluded driver binds it.

questions.question: Do the helpers that cross component files go around their contracts?
questions.answer: No, settled as shared helpers rather than leaks: the agent imports pure formatting and validation helpers and types from the workspace host's files, the workspace and the account import admin-access policy helpers, the admin config's published KV mirror (readAdminConfig) and storage key formats, and Context Library roles import collection-access.ts, the one access rule, and read the registry's published snapshot; none writes or reads another component's store, since each Durable Object's storage is private to its class.

cleanupCandidates.name: Context page mock
cleanupCandidates.why: The /context route is a frosted design mock (ComingSoonPreview) behind a rail entry; the Context Library works through its gatekeeper app instead, so the page is a placeholder waiting to be built or removed (packages/workshop-frontend/src/routes/context.tsx).

cleanupCandidates.name: Legacy observer protocol
cleanupCandidates.why: addObserver, removeObserver and excludeObservers are the old admission protocol, kept beside the kernel's subresource checks until every existing gatekeeper migrates (packages/workshop-backend/src/observer-ledger.ts header; REVIEW.md "Gatekeepers").

cleanupCandidates.name: Frozen workspace-wide use grants
cleanupCandidates.why: Edges and links that granted use of a whole workspace before per-gadget sharing were frozen to the gadgets of their time by a storage migration; links frozen to several gadgets survive as a special case (docs/sharing.md "Frozen workspace-wide use").

cleanupCandidates.name: Grants without a role
cleanupCandidates.why: Edges and share links made before roles existed have no role and are read as build for backwards compatibility (docs/sharing.md "Edges").

cleanupCandidates.name: Legacy connections without a creation spec
cleanupCandidates.why: Old connections without creationSpec cannot verify collaborators, so live admission fails closed for them (docs/sharing.md "Static snapshots").

cleanupCandidates.name: Old GitHub token layout
cleanupCandidates.why: The GitHub account's accessToken and scopes keys are the layout from before expiring grants, migrated on first read and then deleted (packages/gatekeeper-github/storage-schema.md).

cleanupCandidates.name: Unread library record fields
cleanupCandidates.why: Context library records written before sharing still carry a title, description, icon and lastUpdated that nothing reads (packages/gatekeeper-context/src/user-library.ts).

cleanupCandidates.name: Resource types without stable ids
cleanupCandidates.why: Older gatekeepers without resource type ids are still addressed by their URL pattern, a compatibility path (docs/gatekeeper-resource-types.md; gatekeeper.ts startResourceConfigurator).

cleanupCandidates.name: WebSocket abort workaround
cleanupCandidates.why: server.ts detects a lost workspace connection through a disposed callback and closes the WebSocket by hand, marked HACK and TODO until ctx.abort() leaves experimental.

cleanupCandidates.name: Router email handler
cleanupCandidates.why: The router forwards inbound email to an email gatekeeper binding described as dormant until custom domains and Email Routing exist; the handler ships anyway (packages/router/src/index.ts).

excluded.name: Excluded gatekeeper drivers
excluded.why: Sixteen packages for individual outside services, variants of the one driver contract, left out of the corpus by the caller; gatekeeper-github represents them, and they are placed as excluded.

excluded.name: Deploying and configuring an instance
excluded.why: Engineering tooling: the deploy wizard's inputs and release pipeline (scripts/release), worker configs (cloudflare.config.ts) and the environment variables an operator sets, such as ADMINS, AUTH_GATEKEEPERS, CF_AI_GATEWAY and the ADMIN_WORKSPACE bounds, set the system up.

excluded.name: Building, testing and evaluating
excluded.why: Engineering tooling: scripts, CI workflows, the repository's agent skills, the API schema generator, unit and integration tests, and the agent evaluations (scripts, .github, .agents, packages/api-schema, packages/integration-tests, packages/workshop-evals).

excluded.name: Local development
excluded.why: Engineering tooling: pnpm run-local, dev-server and dev-client, and `cf-os api` against a dev server, where anyone may sign in and create password accounts.

excluded.name: Diagnostics
excluded.why: Logging, metrics, tracing, product analytics and frontend error reports (packages/observability, packages/error-reporting, analytics.ts, client-errors.ts, agent-tracing.ts) observe the system rather than serve a consumer.

excluded.name: Version and router probes
excluded.why: Machinery: the version endpoint and the router tag probe let the web app notice a stale session and the backend report a modified router; nobody uses them for a purpose of their own.

excluded.name: Provider behavior
excluded.why: Things the system does on its own, not capabilities: installing bundled blueprints on the first request, directory backfill and revision sync, audit retention pruning, the auto-approval drain, chat cache warming, credential refresh and expiry notices in gatekeepers, retries of hook deliveries and timed update checks.

excluded.name: Gatekeeper kit Layer 2
excluded.why: Documented in plans/gatekeeper-kit.md as KitUserAccountBase, KitVendorBase and KitGatekeeperBase but not shipped; no gatekeeper consumes it (packages/gatekeeper-kit/README.md).

excluded.name: Self-hosting on workerd
excluded.why: The README marks deploying to one's own server on workerd as coming soon; there is no tooling for it in the code.

excluded.name: Plans
excluded.why: plans/ holds design records and proposals; they were read for vocabulary and history only, and the code decided what exists.
